lesson.subtitle: Lesson 10 -- Into It or Over It?
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Giovanna Waltrick | Lesson 10 -- Into It or Over It?

listenings.text: People assume that everybody who comes into a vintage shop is looking for a bargain, and after eleven years behind this counter I can tell you that is not it. They are looking for something nobody else has. That is a completely different thing, and it explains why the cheap rail at the back moves slowly and the strange jacket in the window sells in a day. The other thing I keep noticing is about what lasts. A piece that has already survived thirty years has proved something a new piece simply cannot prove, whatever the label says. And there is one sentence I keep saying to fashion students who come in here, because they all arrive with the same problem. Stop trying to copy an aesthetic you saw online. Start noticing what you already keep wearing, week after week, without deciding to. That is the aesthetic you actually have.

I did not start with any interest in sustainable fashion. I started because I was spending about twenty minutes every single morning standing in front of a full wardrobe deciding what to wear, and I wanted those twenty minutes back. So I picked eleven pieces and I put everything else in a box for six months. Two things surprised me. The first one is how fast the mornings became. Four minutes, no thinking. The second one is the one nobody believes: not one person noticed. Not at university, not at work, not my closest friends. Six months. And what I still avoid doing is telling other people to try it, because it worked for my life, my job and my weather, and it might work for nobody else. If somebody asks, I explain. I stopped announcing it about a week in.
